modb.name: Nova Scotia Mineral Occurrence Database (DP ME 002, version 12, June 2024)
modb.meaning: Mineral-occurrence representative point(s). One occurrence number can have multiple point features; these are not automatically separate mines or openings.
modb.accuracy: The official metadata gives no numeric record accuracy and warns of errors from original collection/GPS and digitizing.

amo.name: Nova Scotia Abandoned Mine Openings Database (DP ME 010, version 9, 2024)
amo.meaning: An individual published abandoned opening point, not a whole mine footprint.
amo.accuracy: Product-level metadata says most Crown-land openings should be within +/-5 m and private-land openings may be up to +/-50 m. This is not a guarantee for a particular record.

method: ArcGIS FeatureServer query using a 2500 metre geodesic distance from each supplied guide point, input spatial reference 4326, output spatial reference 4326; selected related-table queries for MODB evidence.

contradictions.name: MacColls Brook (River Denys Rd) Graphite Occurrence
contradictions.interpretation: Outside the bounded 2.5 km search and much farther from the supplied guide. It is associated spatially with a separate D.J. Beaton opening cluster near Glendale and is not adopted for F19-JUD-103.

contradictions.description: D.J. Beaton graphite adit/decline/shaft cluster near approximately -61.324 longitude, 45.846 to 45.848 latitude.
contradictions.interpretation: Nearby to MODB F14-018 but materially separated from the F19-JUD-103 guide; retained as an alternative historical mining complex, not a match.

empty_result: No MODB graphite representative point occurred within 2.5 km of the guide. GLM-1-001 is the strongest nearby official opening record.
limitations: The saved JSON responses are authoritative service returns. Direct Gesner report pages were also attempted and are linked in mining-records.json, but their noninteractive HTML returned an empty report shell; no unsupported narrative was taken from those pages.
coordinate_correction: Worker summary copied stored Lat_WM84dd/Lon_WM84dd attributes under the query-output label. Final mining-records.json distinguishes both and uses actual returned EPSG:4326 geometry.
